chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Aban, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was the father of guests. So when they were not with him, he would go out seeking them, close his door, take the keys, and go out seeking the guests. And when he returned to his house, he found a man, or someone resembling a man, in the house. So he said: 'O servant of Allah, by whose permission did you enter this house?' He said: 'I entered it by the permission of its Lord.' He repeated that three times. So Ibrahim (peace be upon him) recognized that it was Jibraeel (peace be upon him).

So he (Jibraeel) praised Allah, then said: 'Your Lord has sent me to a servant from His servants to take him as a close friend.' Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'So inform me who he is, so I may serve him until I die.' He said: 'You are he.' He said: 'And why is that so?' He said: 'Because you never asked anyone for anything, and you were never asked for anything, so you said, "No."'

key_terms.أَبَا أَضْيَافٍ: Father of guests (a title for one who frequently hosts)
key_terms.لَمْ تَسْأَلْ أَحَداً شَيْئاً: Did not ask anyone for anything

ai.seo_question: Why was Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) chosen as the close friend of Allah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Prophet Ibrahim’s (AS) profound dignity (‘Izzah) and self-sufficiency, illustrating why he was chosen as Allah’s Khalil (Close Friend). The dialogue emphasizes that his refusal to ask for anything and his state of not being asked for anything reflect a spiritual independence that pleases the Divine, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings on modesty and generosity.
